title_as_printed: Partial Molar Volumes at Infinite Dilution in Water, V2inf, at 298.15 K
pressure_note: total pressure of about 100 kPa (Fortin barometer, +-15 Pa), water saturated with the gas by bubbling at atmospheric pressure; V2 taken as equal to the infinite-dilution value because x2 < 1e-4

value.what: partial molar volume of the dissolved gas at infinite dilution in water, from vibrating-tube density difference (authors' eq 4); the gas mole fraction x2 in eq 4 was calculated from the literature by Henry's law (p.23)

uncertainty.what: average deviation of replicate runs as printed after the plus-minus sign

conversion_needs: paper does not define standard conditions for gas volumes (none used)
notes: Gases outside the seven (argon, krypton, CO, ethylene, acetylene, propylene, cyclopropane, n-butane, 2-methylpropane, 1-butene, 1,3-butadiene, neopentane, methyl chloride) are kept per SPEC. Printed 'value +- uncertainty' split into two columns.
